claims.claim: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $90.0 billion.
Revenue increased 18% compared to the corresponding period of last fiscal year.
Operating income was $40.6 billion.
Operating income increased 18% from the prior year period.
Net income on a GAAP basis was $35.8 billion and increased 31%.
Non-GAAP net income was $35.3 billion and increased 22%.
Diluted earnings per share was $4.81 on a GAAP basis, a 32% increase.
Diluted earnings per share was $4.74 on a non-GAAP basis, a 23% increase.
Microsoft Cloud revenue totaled $59.3 billion, up 27% year over year.
Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43%.
Microsoft Cloud revenue growth was driven by Azure and other cloud services revenue.
claims.note: Causal attribution not in the release. Azure +43% is listed as an Intelligent Cloud segment highlight; the release never states that Azure drove the Microsoft Cloud 27% growth, and gives no Azure dollar figure for the quarter to support the link.

claims.claim: Revenue in Productivity and Business Processes was $37.8 billion, an increase of 14%.
Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue rose 24%.
Revenue in More Personal Computing decreased 4% to $12.9 billion.
Windows OEM and Devices revenue declined 7%.
XBOX content and services revenue dropped 10%.
The More Personal Computing revenue decline was primarily due to the declines in Windows OEM and Devices revenue and XBOX content and services revenue.
claims.note: The release lists these as business highlights without attributing the segment decline to them, and provides no dollar amounts that would establish which drivers were primary.

claims.claim: Microsoft will provide forward-looking guidance in connection with the quarterly earnings announcement on its earnings conference call and webcast.
No specific numerical guidance or outlook figures are provided within the written text of the release.

The company notes that actual results could differ materially due to factors including intense competition, substantial investments in cloud and AI strategy, and evolving legal and regulatory requirements.
Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in dividends and share repurchases during the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026.
Total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments were $76.8 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 84% to $678 billion.
Several discrete items impacted financial results compared with the forward-looking guidance provided on April 29, 2026.
The discrete items included a $3.2 billion gain from an investment in Anthropic and lower-than-expected expenses related to the Voluntary Retirement Program.
Management considers non-GAAP measures in conjunction with GAAP financial results.
Non-GAAP results exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI.
The impact from investments in OpenAI resulted in a net income increase of $480 million for the quarter.
